payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 7. High L1 hit rate is a *bad* sign for streaming workloads (the diagnostic that flips intuition)

problem.statement: CuTeDSL GDN Decode on sm_120 — Pitfalls -- 7. High L1 hit rate is a *bad* sign for streaming workloads (the diagnostic that flips intuition)

payload.attempted: ncu shows L1 hit rate 81% — celebrate, "great cache reuse!"
payload.lesson: For decode/streaming kernels, **L1 hit rate >50% in ncu is a diagnostic of L2 false-saturation**, not of beneficial reuse. Switch to `cpasync.LoadCacheMode.GLOBAL` (skip L1 → DRAM directly). Compare:| Version | L1 hit | L2 throughput | DRAM throughput | Wall-clock | |---|---|---|---|---| | V6 (direct load) | 81% | 96% (saturated) | 34% | 389 μs | | V13 (via cp.async copy) | 33.6% | 81% | 87.7% | **246 μs** |

established_fact.mechanism: Default LDG `.ca` cache mode pulls every load through L1. For streaming workloads (T=1 decode, no inter-iteration reuse), the L1 just gets filled and re-evicted. The "hit" is really **redundant LDGs serviced by in-flight L1 lines from the same kernel**, doubling L2 traffic and saturating the L2 throughput long before DRAM. The kernel looks "BW-bound" but on the wrong unit.

payload.observed: Memory throughput stuck at 411 GB/s; L2 throughput 96% saturated; DRAM throughput only 34%. Kernel is 1.58× slower than FLA Triton despite "good cache hits".
